newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU adopts law on electricity liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: EU adopts law on electricity liberalisation.

text.p: The European Union formally ended years of wrangling on Friday by adopting a law liberalising the bloc's giant electricity markets.

Fisheries ministers meeting in Brussels adopted the law without discussion, an EU official said. They were able to do this because last week the European Parliament approved the draft without proposing further changes.
The new rules are expected to come into force in January once they have been published in the EU's Official Journal.
EU energy ministers reached a compromise on the controversial dossier last June after six years of wrangling, but the parliament had to give its opinion before it could be formally adopted.
Under the deal, nearly a quarter of the EU's market will be open to competition from January 1999. This will rise to about a third by 2003.
The Netherlands, which takes over the presidency of the EU in January, hopes to finalise by July 1997 a draft directive which will introduce competition also into the EU gas market.
